title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + compaction to reduce fragmentation and spillover
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory fragmentation and spillover behavior by introducing an adaptive eviction scorer, background compaction/defragmentation, and safer paging heuristics. Reduces OOMs under high-concurrency workloads and lowers spillover to host memory and disk.
description: Motivation: We observe frequent KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover into host DRAM and paging under bursty multi-tenant workloads. This causes increased latency tail and occasional OOMs on dense GPU nodes. This PR implements an adaptive eviction policy and a lightweight compaction path to reduce fragmentation, improve reuse locality, and reduce paging/spillover. Summary of changes: - Add adaptive eviction scorer that combines recency, token-cost, allocation-fragmentation score, and the expected future reuse probability (LRU + cost-aware heuristics). - Introduce a background compaction/defragmentation job that coalesces small free segments and reduces allocation churn without blocking the hot request path. Compaction runs conservatively based on free-fragment thresholds and memory pressure signals. - Safer spillover/paging heuristics: we now prefer spilling cold, large contiguous entries and avoid splitting large hot segments. When host spillover is necessary we mark spilled segments with a retry/backoff policy to prevent repeated synchronous fetches. - Scheduler integration: eviction and compaction are coordinated with the request scheduler so we avoid compaction during critical latency windows and use a token to serialize heavy memory operations. - Telemetry and guards: new metrics for fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs, adaptive_evictions, spill_events, and per-tenant eviction_cost. Added alerts to surface regressed fragmentation and spillover. Implementation notes: The hot path (lookup/insert) remains lock-minimal. The adaptive eviction scorer uses a small per-shard histogram to estimate reuse and a lightweight bloom to guess coldness; this avoids full access logs. Compaction runs on dedicated background workers and uses an epoch-based memory reclamation to avoid races with ongoing KV readers. Backwards compatibility: config knobs are feature-gated and off by default for customers on dedicated clusters; rollout controlled by canary flag. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2142) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Performance tests (bench harness) - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert rules - [x] Canary rollout plan - [x] Docs update (runtime tuning) Notes: See the design doc for tuning guidance. This PR aims to be conservative: defaults reduce spillover in our internal perf lab by ~35% p95 memory usage and cut tail latency regression in stress tests.

notes_for_release: Enabled by default in hosted canary clusters after 1 week. Config knobs: kv_cache.adaptive_eviction.enabled, kv_cache.compaction.threshold, kv_cache.spillover.strategy. Recommended default: keep adaptive_eviction.enabled=true, compaction.threshold=0.12 (fragmentation ratio) for GPU nodes with >256GB host DRAM. See docs/runtime/kv-cache.md for tuning.
bench_results_summary: Internal perf lab: stress-multi-tenant scenario (1000 concurrent contexts): fragmentation_ratio reduced from 0.38 -> 0.12, host spill events -35% p95 GPU memory usage -28%, tail latency (99th) improved by ~12%. CPU overhead for compaction kept under 4% while running at low priority.
notes: This is an iterative improvement; follow-ups planned: - per-tenant eviction priority (ENG-2198) - on-disk spill format optimization - dynamic shard rebalancer if fragmentation persists
